information.description:
True to their nickname, Dragons spit fire from large-caliber weaponry and have magical (cybernetic) abilities well above most gangers. They’re often used as heavy-duty hitmen or bodyguards for when muscle and blades alone won’t cut it.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Tyger Claws).

description.value: Experts in combat who use their fighting prowess to dominate in the lawless time of the Red.

This classic rifle manufactured at the dawn of the century possesses a unique shape, design and color-scheme that delivers a clear message to enemy targets and rivals alike: I am Death incarnate. Even today, more than a half-century after its conception, this rifle commands respect on the battlefield and on the city streets.

Cost: 250eb (Expensive)

Class: Assault Rifle • Skill: Shoulder Arms • Range: Battle Rifle

Damage: 5d6 • Capacity: 21 • ROF: 1 • Hands: 2

Alt. Firing Modes: None

Concealable: No

Slots: 2 • Attachments: Battle Barrel • Mods: None

Special Features: Has 1 less Attachment Slot (2 Total). Expends 3 rounds in a burst when fired. Whenever this weapon would ablate armor, it ablates 1 additional SP (2 SP Normal / 3 SP Armor Piercing). This weapon will not fire if there are less than 3 rounds in the magazine.

Range: Battle Rifle
Pre-installed: Battle Barrel (effects already included in these stats)

Foundry notes:

  • Its range tables come from this module's DV Tables compendium; run the module's "Use Corgo's 77 DV Tables" macro once per world (see the module README).

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Weapons > Weapon Catalog).

One of the oldest weapons made by Arasaka from the early 2000s. These days it's a rare sight on the street, as it's a pistol that is — no point in sugarcoating it — outdated and difficult to maintain. Spare parts for it are no longer manufactured, and it's no longer compatible with most standard weapon mods. That being said, should it be held up to someone's head and have its trigger is pulled, the end result will still be as conclusive as with any modern firearm.

Cost: 100eb (Premium)

Class: Very Heavy Pistol • Skill: Handgun • Range: Pistol

Damage: 4d6 • Capacity: 8 • ROF: 1 • Hands: 1

Alt. Firing Modes: None

Concealable: No

Slots: 2 • Attachments: None • Mods: None

Special Features: Armor-Piercing Ammunition bought for this weapon costs 20eb (Everyday) per 10, and can only be used by this weapon.

Range: Pistol

The modern Kerenzikov takes the place of the now defunct Reflex Co-Processor to help reduce the strain on the user's Neuroport.

Neuralware. The user can now dodge Ranged Attacks if they could not do so already, and gain a +2 bonus to Checks for noticing Ambushes.

NOTE: Credit to Infernox_Ratchet for the basis of this item.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital

  • Replaces the core system's Kerenzikov; use this one instead of the core item.
  • The +2 is on Perception and situational, because it only applies to noticing an Ambush: tick it in the roll dialog.

Cost: 500eb (Expensive) ♦ Install: Clinic

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6)

Run the edge at top speed, choomba. There ain’t another way to live.

Speedware. As an Action, the user may activate this cyberware, after which it remains active for the next 60 seconds (20 Rounds). While active, this cyberware provides a +3 bonus to any Initiative Roll made. If activated while the user is already in an Initiative Queue, their current Initiative increases by 3, which is lost if this cyberware deactivates or its duration expires during combat. This cyberware has a 1 hour cooldown before it can be activated again. Only 1 piece of Speedware can be installed at a time.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Clinic
Option Slots: uses 1

Foundry notes:

  • Replaces the core system's Sandevistan; use this one instead of the core item.
  • Matches the core item's setup: the +3 shows as a toggle in the initiative roll dialog.
